Stop babysitting your AI coding assistant with endless manual prompts. 🤖⚙️

If you are tired of AI forgetting your project conventions, writing hallucinated bugs, or breaking your codebase during multi-file updates, it is time to upgrade your setup. 

Meet ECC: an agent harness operating system that turns AI coding assistants into disciplined engineers through persistent memory, automated validation, and continuous learning. 🚀

ECC solves the infrastructure bottleneck of managing agent memory, execution safety, and workflows in modern AI environments like Claude Code and Cursor. Instead of ad-hoc prompting, it enforces a strict engineering loop of planning, testing, implementing, reviewing, and remembering.

Here is what makes ECC a game-changer for your workflow:
• 71 Specialized Agents: Comprehensive ecosystem for planning, security, architecture, and build repair.
• 314 Built-in Skills: Massive library covering TDD, deep research, documentation, frontend development, and operations.
• Persistent Memory Optimization: Preserves crucial project context without bloating your active token window.
• AgentShield Security: Robust scanning to ensure safe, reliable execution across your development environments.

Enforce strict Test-Driven Development where your agent automatically writes, verifies, and repairs unit tests before finalizing code, and offload complex architecture reviews to specialized sub-agents. 

Stop re-explaining your stack and start shipping reliable, secure code today. 💻✨

Tired of babysitting your CLI AI coding assistant? 🛑

Tools like Claude Code and Codex are incredible, but they share one major flaw: they force you to sit there manually watching the terminal and supplying continuous prompts just to get things done. 

Meet Agent Autoloop (https://github.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop) — an ultra-lightweight, self-hosted automation middle-tier that lets CLI AI agents handle background tasks autonomously, only interrupting you when high-friction approvals are actually needed. 🚀

Turn your local AI toolsets into 24/7 background automation workers for routine tasks like triaging GitHub issues, running website health checks, generating morning briefings, and executing code reviews—all without renting heavy cloud infrastructure.

Key features built for developers:
⚙️ Zero-Dependency Core: Event-sourced with event tracing and disk-backed consistency so it stays reliable even if the process abruptly terminates.
🔌 Zero-SDK Integration: Works seamlessly with any command-line agent that accepts prompts and outputs terminal text, including Claude Code, Codex, ACP, and DeepSeek Harness.
🔔 Multi-Channel Escalation: Routes human-in-the-loop decisions and approval cards directly to Slack, Discord, Feishu, DingTalk, or desktop notifications.
🛡️ Built-In Guardrails: Includes a hop-count circuit breaker (TTL mechanism) and strict command-data separation to block unsafe prompt injection from external events.

Stop wasting hours staring at terminal windows and let your AI work asynchronously while you focus on high-level architecture.

👉 Check out the repo and star it here: https://github.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop

Tired of awkward recording bots cluttering your global tech syncs and live streams? Meet Cicada—the open-source utility designed to break down language barriers instantly on your desktop and mobile devices. 🎙️✨

Cicada captures system audio and microphone inputs locally, delivering real-time bilingual subtitles, automated AI meeting notes, and seamless simultaneous interpretation without inviting invasive third-party bots into your calls. 

Here is what makes Cicada a must-have for developers and international teams:

🚀 Native Audio Capture: Utilizes local speech recognition and speaker diarization via Core ML and embedded models like WeSpeaker ResNet34-LM on Apple Silicon Macs.
🌐 Flexible AI Backends: Easily integrate with Ling, OpenRouter, ZenMux, or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints for high-level translations and voice cloning.
🗣️ Push-to-Talk Interpretation: Route translated speech directly into virtual audio drivers like BlackHole for smooth, real-time cross-lingual communication.
🔒 Local-First Architecture: Your raw recordings, transcripts, and notes stay securely on your device, with robust cross-platform support across macOS, Windows, Linux, and Android.

For developers, the codebase is a high-performance reference implementation built with native Swift/SwiftUI, showcasing local-first audio processing, Core ML integration, virtual audio driver piping, and custom AI service failover chains.

Explore the codebase and start building today:
https://github.com/wquguru/cicada

How an autonomous AI penetration testing legion outperformed human-engineered setups while consuming 78% fewer tokens through multi-agent orchestration and layered graph memory. 🚀

Building long-running autonomous systems usually means hitting a wall of context degradation, token bloat, and agent crashes. 

sapper-v2 is an advanced autonomous penetration testing and multi-agent orchestration framework built for competitive attack-defense scenarios. It solves long-horizon AI task execution by replacing single monolithic agents with a coordinated swarm consisting of a commander, scouts, generals, and soldiers, backed by a persistent layered fact-intent graph. 🛡️

✨ Key Features:
• Multi-Agent Orchestration Harness: Dynamically spawns, manages, and coordinates various AI agents and models inside tmux sessions, enabling division of labor like human civil societies.
• Layered Fact-Intent Graph Memory: Implements a structured external memory system (title, summary, evidence) that prevents context degradation, avoids information poisoning, and allows agent successors to resume interrupted tasks.
• Economic Model Tiering: Combines high-capability reasoning models for top-level strategy with fast, lightweight models for mass execution, drastically lowering token consumption.
• Emergent Capabilities: Demonstrates self-organizing behaviors during unattended runs, such as generating dedicated sub-roles (like signalmen for flag submission) and enforcing operational doctrines.

🛠️ Developer Value:
Extract the underlying multi-agent coordination mechanics to build resilient, long-horizon automation workflows for engineering, research, and complex system administration. It provides a blueprint for managing agent crashes, state handovers, and cost-effective model tiering outside of isolated chat prompts.

Check out the repository here:

Tired of bloated, Electron-based note apps that chew through your RAM and lag when you paste a massive code block? 

Meet Quiet.md: a blazing-fast, local-first notes application built with Rust and GPUI that ditches WebViews entirely for native GPU rendering. 

🔥 The Problem It Solves:
Modern note-taking apps are sluggish, memory-heavy, and lock your data in proprietary clouds. Quiet.md fixes this by giving you a high-performance, GPU-accelerated native desktop client. It stores your work locally as individual files using the Feishu (Lark) DocxXML format, meaning you keep total ownership and can track everything seamlessly with Git.

⚡ Standout Features:
• Sub-6ms Frame Processing: Built with Rust and GPUI to handle million-character documents without breaking a sweat.
• 100% Local-First: Zero mandatory background services, zero telemetry, and complete offline capability.
• Rich Developer-Focused Formatting: Natively supports tables, callouts, LaTeX math, and code blocks.
• Customizable Theming: Pre-built styles matching tools like Obsidian and Notion, plus custom CSS injection support.

Whether you are a Rust developer looking for a production-grade reference implementation for building complex GUI apps with GPUI, or a technical writer demanding a lightning-fast workspace, Quiet.md is worth a star on GitHub.

👉 Check it out and explore the source code here: https://github.com/s1dashu/quiet-md
